articleTitle: A Non-Iterative LMI-Based Design of Static Output Feedback Control with $\mathcal{L}_{2}$ Gain Performance for Linear Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: In this paper, we present a new LMI-based non-iterative design strategy for static output feedback controllers with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{L}_{2}$</tex> Gain Performance for linear systems. In our approach, on the basis of the well-known necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of the static output feedback control for linear systems, the non-iterative LMI-based design procedure for the proposed static output feedback controller is derived. In this paper, we show the LMI-based non-iterative design procedure for static output feedback controllers with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{L}_{2}$</tex> Gain Performance and the effectiveness of the proposed static output feedback control is presented through a simple illustrative example.

articleTitle: Optimal Energy Mix Modeling Simulation Using Reinforcement Learning on Philippine Monthly Energy Utilization for 2020–2022
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: A traditional method of generating an optimal energy mix involves selecting from various power producers, each with different costs per kilowatt-hour (kWh). This energy is then transmitted and distributed among various end-user sectors. However, this study explores a novel approach by replacing the traditional involvement of transmission and distribution utilities with reinforcement learning (RL) techniques. The objective was to determine an optimal energy mix over a 36-month period in the Philippines, from 2020 to 2022. The study evaluated several RL methods, including Q-learning, Deep Q-Network (DQN), Double Q-learning, and Actor-Critic algorithms. Each algorithm was tested with different learning rates <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\alpha)$</tex> and discount factors <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\gamma)$</tex> to find the most effective combination. Among these, the Actor-Critic algorithm, with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha=0.10$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma=0.90$</tex>, emerged as the most optimal. The simulations showed that using each algorithm, no energy demand in kWh was left unmet, demonstrating its effectiveness in managing and optimizing energy distribution. This approach not only automated the decision-making process but also enhanced efficiency by continuously learning and adapting to changes in energy production and consumption patterns.

articleTitle: A Multi-Port Power Converter with High Voltage Gain
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: This paper proposes a multi-port power converter (MPC) that integrates fuel cells (FC) and energy storage batteries, featuring high voltage gain capable of supplying high voltage to loads or DC microgrids. Based on the battery's state of charge/discharge control and protection, and load power requirements, the converter operates in three different modes. To optimize implementation cost, size, and modularity, the converter design includes an energy storage inductor integrated with an auxiliary boost circuit, which enhances voltage gain, reduces stress on power components, and improves conversion efficiency. The content of this paper includes circuit topology analysis, circuit simulation, and steady-state analysis, culminating in the development of a 500W prototype platform. Experimental and simulation results verify the feasibility of the proposed system, achieving maximum efficiencies of 98.7%, 98.7%, and 98.5% in the three modes, respectively.

articleTitle: Exploiting Connection-Switching U-Net for Enhancing Surface Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Surface defect detection in manufacturing is essen-tial but challenging due to data imbalance from the rarity of abnormal data. To address this, unsupervised anomaly detection (UAD) has been widely adopted, which trains reconstruction Neural Networks (NNs) with normal samples only. Recent studies have focused on reconstruction-by-inpainting approaches, evolving from multi-random masking to single deterministic masking strategies in order to maximize UAD performance without changing the NN structure. Single deterministic masking methods use 1) an U-Net structure to reduce false positives through precise normal pattern reconstruction and 2) an identity shortcut (IS) to avoid increasing false negatives by partially masking the input image. We investigate into further improvement of U-Net based UAD models without training or modifying their NN structure. To achieve performance improvement, we propose connection-Switching U-Net (CS-U-Net) that is trained with fully activated skip connections and then selectively deactivates some of the connections during inference to mitigate IS issues. This simple scheme effectively contains the generalization ability of deployed UAD models to reconstruct abnormal patterns into normal patterns. Using the KolektorSDD2 dataset, we have verified that our method achieves better throughput than state-of-the-art methods, suggesting its potential to be used as a widely adopted inference strategy for UAD where contained generalization ability is necessary.

articleTitle: Designing an Early Flood Warning System Using SRF05 and S201 Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: In recent years, natural disasters and floods have occurred more frequently and at a more serious level, causing serious damage to people, property, and the ecological environment. Reducing damage caused by floods is an extremely urgent issue that many organizations and scientists worldwide are focusing on researching. Flood is the natural disasters and the result of the process of concentrating water in large quantities and overflowing into low-lying areas, causing widespread flooding. It causes not only heavy damage to people and property but also long-term negative impacts on the ecological environment. Floods have complex and unpredictable developments. They occur continuously every year and are too difficult to control. The damage that they cause is huge. This paper first aims to design a flood warning system that can operate under harsh weather conditions. Our system uses two sensors (SRF05 and S201) to measure level and flow of water. We also design the server to receive data from the system. They are compared with the measurement results, which are given warnings and uploaded on the web, helping everyone to monitor the flood situation quickly. The simulation results proves that the system is able to detect water levels from 70 cm to 100 cm in real time which can be applied in practice.

articleTitle: GPU-Enhanced PDE Solver Simulating Information Processing in Mach-Zehnder Interferometer
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Numerical methods are essential for simulating transient physical phenomena, providing crucial support to engineers and researchers in fields such as defense, space, and the natural sciences. By modeling these phenomena with partial differential equations (PDEs), deeper insights can be gained. Among the various PDE-solving methods, the Crank-Nicolson technique stands out for its efficiency in handling time-dependent PDEs, offering precise and stable solutions across diverse applications. In this work, we present a 3<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex> GPU-accelerated code optimized for parallel execution in three-dimensional space-time domains. The PDE solver is applied to quantum wave function information processing, specifically in the context of the circular double-slit experiment. Additionally, we utilize the solver to simulate a dual Mach-Zehnder interferometer to model the Fenna-Matthews-Olson (FMO) complex, developing a nature-inspired algorithm based on its quantum dynamics. This simulation demonstrates near-perfect intelligence in a photosynthetic system without any neural network. This work may help in the design of solar cells, potentially increasing their efficiency to a greater extent.

articleTitle: A Proposal for Security Training Tools in Building Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: In today's information society, building systems integrated and managed by IP networks are becoming more common. However, there are many network devices, Internet of Things (IoT) devices, and other terminals in building systems, and the possibility that IoT malware such as “Mirai” could adversely affect the entire building is well foreseeable. Therefore, there is an urgent need to properly operate defenses against this problem in order to establish secure building systems. In addition, since there are precedents where damage has increased due to delays in responding to security incidents, training that assumes IoT malware has infiltrated a building is also necessary to familiarize security personnel. In this paper, we propose a training tool that uses Mirai, one of the IoT malware, and assumes that a terminal infected with Mirai has infiltrated a building. In particular, focusing on the communication and spreading functions of Mirai, we propose a safe training environment by installing actual bots as Mirai-infected terminals in a building system, a command and control (CnC) server that issues commands to the bots, and a loader that downloads malware to new terminals in a virtual environment. A secure training environment and training scenarios are then created. Furthermore, using the prototype training tool, we confirmed that it is possible to reproduce security incidents and conduct response training in an environment that mimics actual building systems. As a result, it is now possible to conduct incident response training based on a series of scenarios in a secure training environment, reproducing security incidents in an environment similar to an actual building system, which has been difficult in the past.

articleTitle: A Robust Guaranteed Cost Formation Control for a Class of Uncertain Multi-Agent Systems for Event-Trigger-Based Variable Gain Controllers
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a design method for a new event-trigger-based variable gain robust controller which achieves both consensus and guaranteed cost performance for a class of uncertain multi-agent systems (MASs) with the leader-follower structure. The proposed variable gain robust controller is composed of stabilizing state feedback laws, state feedback inputs for consensus, and compensation inputs with adjustable parameters, and is designed for giving consideration to relative positions explicitly. In this paper, we show that sufficient conditions for the existence of the proposed robust guaranteed cost formation controller are given in terms of Linear Matrix Inequalities (LMIs). Finally, a simple example is included.

articleTitle: Frequency Stability in Renewable-Rich Power Systems with High Solar Ramps
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: The rapid integration of renewable energy sources into power systems is outpacing the implementation of solutions to address the stability challenges they pose. This study focuses on the impact of rapid ramp-down incidences of solar power plants on the stability of isolated power systems with high non-conventional renewable energy penetration and minimal support from thermal plants. Key issues include the intermittency of renewables, reduction of system inertia, and unpredicted ramp events. By using a simulated scenario based on the IEEE 14 bus system, comprising hydro and solar generation plants, this research identifies the maximum ramp-down rate and duration that the system can withstand without compromising stability. Hydro power plants, with their flexible and quick response capabilities, are critical for frequency control and system stabilization. Solar power plants, representing the most widely used non-conventional renewable source, add variability to the system. The simulation involves adjusting the irradiation levels of a 280MW solar power plant to model various ramp-down scenarios, using PSCAD software to observe system frequency behavior. The study tests multiple ramp rates and durations to determine the threshold at which the system frequency drops to 49.5Hz, the minimum acceptable frequency for a 50Hz system. The findings provide valuable insights into the ramp rate tolerance of renewable-rich isolated power systems, offering guidance for enhancing system stability amidst increasing renewable energy penetration. This research underscores the importance of strategic planning and implementation of responsive control mechanisms to ensure the reliable operation of future power systems.

articleTitle: Research on Fine Management Path and Digital Platform of LCA Carbon Emissions in Building Structure Life Cycle Based on Low-Carbon AIoT Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: With the increasingly severe global climate change, “peak carbon dioxide emissions” and “carbon neutrality” have become the common concern of the international community. As one of the main sources of greenhouse gas emissions, the construction industry's lowcarbon transformation is particularly urgent. This study focuses on the low-carbon intelligent and healthy AIoT management system for building space, relying on four types of digital carbon management platforms, and discusses the process of realizing the fine management of LCA carbon emissions in the whole life cycle of building structures. The research results provide theoretical support and practical guidance for the low-carbon development of the construction industry.

articleTitle: Automated Architectural Control: Implementing the Governance as Code
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Governance as Code (GaC) is an emerging approach aimed at automating software architectural control within the modern software engineering industry. This article addresses the challenges associated with software architectural control and presents the generalized GaC approach as a solution that enables the transformation of the architectural control process from a theoretical framework into an automated, practical tool for ensuring compliance with engineering and security standards. The implementation of GaC is structured around three key tasks: representing software architecture as a universal formal model, performing reverse engineering to extract software architecture from ready-to-deploy systems, and automating the verification of architectural control rules. For each of these tasks, a solution is provided along with the underlying motivations.

articleTitle: Compact Data Learning For Time-Series Forecasting Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: This paper focuses on optimizing machine learning-based time-series forecasting models by constructing compact data. Methods for optimizing ML training have been improved and integrated into the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems. Compact Data Learning (CDL) serves as an alternative practical framework to optimize machine learning (ML) systems by reducing the size of the sampling data. This framework originated from compact data design, providing optimal assets without handling complex big data. Compact Data Learning for Time-Series (CDL-TS) is a novel framework aimed at minimizing forecasting model errors. By utilizing reduced sampling and robust comparison procedures, CDL-TS addresses the challenges of forecasting models on extensive real-time data systems. Additionally’ an analytic solution for the M/M/1 queueing system with continuous time parameters under finite time limits is presented in this research. The major contributions are valuable insights and practical techniques for improving model training efficiency, particularly in reducing data volume for continuous time-series data.

articleTitle: PLC based Industrial Power Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: The traditional manual change-overs during the time of power cut-off and voltage instability are time-consuming, can damage machinery, and endanger lives. A power management system enhances plant safety by ensuring power and steam for critical loads and preventing blackouts. Traditional use of relays in industries required manual operations, resulting in degraded output quality. PLCs offer reliability, flexibility, and accuracy to automation systems. This paper describes the project that aims to design and implement automatic power switching between an incoming power line and a backup source during line cut-offs, over-voltage, and under-voltage conditions, and switch back to the main line once stable. The system is monitored and controlled via HMI and PLC, eliminating issues like over-voltage, under-voltage, and complete power shutdowns.

articleTitle: An Integrated Single-Phase to Three-Phase Wireless AC Motor Drive System Connected to Class-E/F3 Inverter and S-S Resonance Compensation Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: This paper introduces a wireless AC motor drive system operating in a single-stage/single-phase to three-phase configuration. The transmitter (Tx) employs a Class-E/F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> resonant inverter design, which effectively reduces switching current and voltage stress, thereby amplifying output power and enhancing reliability. The receiver (Rx) utilizes a novel wireless AC motor drive topology capable of directly converting singlephase AC power to three-phase AC output, efficiently powering AC motors. Numerical analysis demonstrates that the proposed system achieves a power transfer efficiency of 94.39%.

articleTitle: Roughness Analysis of Stainless Steel Bearing Using Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Current technology utilizes a sophisticated standard room measurement system to analyze the average roughness of Stainless Steel Bearing Surface. However, this process relies on random sampling at infrequent intervals, resulting in inefficiency and inadequate analysis of a large number of samples. To address this issue, we propose a solution using computer vision via laser scanning. The scanning process produces an amplified speckle pattern of the ring surface. This pattern is then analyzed to verify the number of edges that cross a predefined threshold and exhibit symmetrical patterns, particularly on smoothed ring surfaces. Remarkably, this system operates with a turnaround time of less than a second. Moreover, unlike the standard room setup, this technology can be seamlessly integrated directly into production/manufacturing units.

articleTitle: Battery Refurbishment Technologies in Industry 4.0: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: The increasing demand for batteries in various industries has resulted in the problem of battery waste. An industry 4.0 will need to tackle this kind of environmental problem. With the need for a more sustainable solution, battery refurbishment technologies have emerged as a way to reduce the environmental impact of battery waste, conserve resources, and save costs. In this review, we will discuss the existing battery refurbishment technologies in the world, including their advantages and disadvantages. The authors also discussed about their current battery refurbishment project with the help of artificial intelligence.

articleTitle: Selection of Negative Correlative Pairs to Build an Annual Rebalancing Portfolio
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Portfolio management of mutual funds and exchange-traded funds is an essential issue for investors and managers. The task of portfolio management is asset allocation and maintenance over time. Modern portfolio theory (i.e., mean-variance analysis) is the mainstream method for asset allocation, and rebalancing is to maintain the allocation over time. Compared with mean-variance analysis, Hierarchical risk parity (HRP) is a stable and state-of-the-art method to build a portfolio. However, those methods did not take rebalancing into consideration. The mechanism of rebalancing maintains the portfolio by selling those securities that have gone up and buying those securities prices that have gone down. Rebalancing of negative corrective pairs of securities implies a buy-low and sellhigh strategy. Therefore, this research adopts HRP and combines annual rebalancing with negative correlative pairs of securities to maximize portfolio return. The results showed that the proposed method outperformed portfolios built by vanilla HRP and genetic algorithm.

articleTitle: High-Capacity DWDM Transmission System for Free-Space Optical Network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: This study presents the architecture and performance evaluation of a high-capacity free-space optical (FSO) communication system that makes use of dense wavelength division multiplexing (DWDM) and a 1.28 Tb/s link. The system under consideration comprises 64 individual channels, each of which is capable of transferring data streams at a speed of 20 Gbps. A return-to-zero (RZ) line coding algorithm is incorporated to maximize performance across 2.0 km of FSO link. Important parameters that affect the system's performance, like beam divergence and atmosphere attenuation, are taken into account in the analysis. The signals' bit-error-rate (BER), quality factor (Q), and eye diagrams are calculated and examined to assess the system's performance. For future optical-wireless networks that require significant bandwidth capabilities, cost-effective implementation, and increased flexibility, this novel high-capacity design offers a promising solution. The results aid in the development of dependable and useful high-speed FSO communication systems.

articleTitle: Benchmarking Variational Autoencoders for Dimensionality Reduction and Application to Medical Heartbeats Data
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: This report explores the implementation of Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) for dimensionality reduction in multivariate statistics. We benchmark VAEs against traditional methods such as PCA, ICA, and KPCA, using datasets including Iris Flowers, Wine, and Breast Cancer. The study further extends the application of VAEs to non-columnar data, specifically medical heartbeat audio recordings. The results demonstrate the strengths and limitations of VAEs in clustering, manifold learning, and anomaly detection, particularly in the context of medical data. Our findings suggest that while VAEs offer flexible nonlinear representations, their performance is highly sensitive to the type of activation function used and the nature of the data.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Based Detection and Classification of Gastrointestinal Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Detecting diseases and abnormalities in the gastrointestinal tract poses a significant challenge for healthcare professionals and can greatly impact treatment. Deep learning has become increasingly important in the analysis of medical images, helping with diagnosis, disease prediction, and treatment evaluation. Several research studies have utilized CNNs to accurately classify medical images. However, current techniques for identifying gastrointestinal abnormalities often utilize intricate architectures that necessitate extensive parameter tuning. This underscores the need for a streamlined deep learning approach that is easily replicable while maintaining the high accuracy of more intricate models. This research introduces a methodology for classifying gastrointestinal diseases and anomalies using image processing and a transfer learning technique. Leveraging deep learning methods, our objective is to develop an advanced and precise model for predicting diseases.

articleTitle: Detachable and Portable Moisture Sensors for Industrial Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: This paper presents the design, fabrication and testing of an innovative moisture analyzer with a detachable and portable moisture sensor, which can compensate for both bulk density and temperature effects, thus allowing to detect the moisture content in granulates at real time with a precision of 20 ppm and a sensitivity at room temperature of 37.5 fF/ppm. Experimental results obtained from moisture measurements with polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polyamide 66 (PA66) and polycarbonate (PC) are reported thus making it possible to use it in a wide range of industrial applications.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Variable Gain Robust State Observer for a Class of Uncertain Nonlinear Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: This paper proposes a new variable gain robust state observer for a class of uncertain nonlinear systems. The variable gain robust state observer proposed in this paper consists of fixed observer gain matrices and nonlinear modification functions which are determined by appropriate updating rules. It is shown that sufficient conditions for the existence of the proposed variable gain robust state observer can be reduced to solvability of Linear Matrix Inequalities (LMIs). Finally, we give a simple numerical example.

articleTitle: An MILP Based Energy Optimization in a Multi Source EV Charging Station
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: The global rise in Electric Vehicle (EV) adoption to reduce the carbon footprint has intensified the need for efficient energy management strategies in grid-connected EV charging stations. This paper presents an optimal energy management approach using Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) to maximize the profit for the charging station owners (CSOs), a key factor in driving further investment in the charging infrastructure and accelerating widespread adoption of EVs. By leveraging MILP, the proposed framework enables charging station operators to optimize EV charging schedules, accounting for dynamic time-of-use (TOU) electricity rates, PV generation variability, and fluctuating EV demand. The objective is to maximize profit while ensuring sustainable and cost-effective operation. Simulation results highlight the effectiveness of this approach in improving profitability and reducing operational costs. The study underscores the potential of MILP to enhance the efficiency and sustainability of EV charging infrastructure, accelerating the shift towards smart and resilient urban mobility solutions.

articleTitle: PCA-Based Vehicle Size Estimation in High-Resolution MIMO FMCW Radar System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new approach to simultaneously estimate the length and width of the vehicle ahead using a high-resolution automotive frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar sensor. First, the point cloud data is generated by detecting a moving vehicle ahead using a high-resolution FMCW radar. The proposed vehicle size estimation method is based on the principal component analysis (PCA). The length and width of the target are estimated by orthogonally projecting each point onto the eigenvectors of the point cloud data obtained using the PCA method. The length and width of the target estimated using the proposed method results in average error rate of 2.18 % and 2.51 %, respectively. Furthermore, the efficiency of the proposed method has been validated under the presence of substantial road noise, demonstrating its robustness and reliability in traffic applications.

articleTitle: Fine-Tuning TMDDPG for Dynamic IIoT Bandwidth Allocation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: The advancement of Industrial IoT (IIoT) calls for devices that can provide fast communication, for real time operations. Ensuring Quality of Service (QoS) for devices in a network requires effective management of bandwidth. Traditional fixed allocation methods struggle to meet changing needs. This study examines how Software Defined Networking (SDN) with network slicing can tackle this issue. Network slicing divides the network into segments each tailored to QoS needs. In this context we suggest a system that uses a Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm based on Fine-tuned transfer learning for allocating bandwidth in network slices, for IIoT devices requiring ultra reliable low latency communication. This strategy uses knowledge from existing ML model to optimize allocation and reduce training time and computational resources.

articleTitle: Impact Analysis of Low Carbon Technologies for Residential Buildings in Hot Summer and Cold Winter Regions
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: The construction industry has become a key area of emission reduction action due to its huge energy consumption and significant proportion of carbon emissions. The development of ultra-low energy buildings is in line with China's policy of “peak carbon dioxide emissions carbon neutrality”. To investigate the technical system and economic scheme of ultra-low-energy-consumption residential buildings suitable for hot summer and cold winter regions, this study takes a model house in Jiujiang City, Jiangxi Province, as a research object, establishes a typical residential model, and analyzes the effects of external walls, external windows, sunshades and ventilation forms on energy consumption. The incremental cost of ultra-low energy consumption residences was discussed, and the popularization value of ultra-low energy consumption buildings in hot summer and cold winter regions was analyzed.

articleTitle: Smart Reverse Vending Machines: Integrating Deep Learning and IOT for Enhanced Recycling
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Plastics pollution is thereby a major danger to both the land and aquatic life system because of their frequent application. When it comes to wastes, then plastic bottles, cans, milk cartoons are some of the worst products that take many years to decompose hence polluting the environment. The proposed system of this paper is an improved RVM(Reverse Vending Machine) that encompasses the use of Deep Learning (DL), and Internet of Things(IoT) technologies to improve the efficiency of recycling. Realtime object detection and recognition is done by the YOLO (You Only Look Once) V10, it distinguishes between plastics, cans, and milk cartons. A Flutter-based application enables the user interface, while Firebase handles users' record and synchronization of activities. Further, brand detection is done using Google Cloud Vision API to gather information about the trends in recycling. The IoT framework of the system helps track bin storage levels to avoid efficiently inciting waste collection. This paper outlines the RVM system's general layout, functioning and effectiveness, proving that it has the potential to revolutionize the recycling practice and promote environmental preservation.

articleTitle: pFedKD: Personalized Federated Learning Meet Knowledge Distillation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Traditional Federated Learning (FL) ensures privacy and security by letting clients jointly learn a model without sharing data with other clients. However, statistical heterogeneity caused each client to have an unsatisfactory personalization ability. To mitigate the problem, we propose pFedKD in this paper, a personalized Federated Learning algorithm with knowledge distillation. During FL training, pFedKD identifies the optimal round with the best local accuracy for each client as the teacher model for knowledge distillation while treating the final round as the student model. Then, the knowledge distillation module extracts desired information for each client's local model, ensuring the accuracy and efficiency of pFedKD. Finally, our extensive experiments on Cifar10 outperform vanilla FedAvg, FedProx, and other SOTA personalized FL algorithms by at least 1.2%, underscoring the superiority of pFedKD.

articleTitle: Autonomous Flight Implementation of Flapping Wing Aerial Vehicle with Data Driven Mathematical Modal Formation using Wireless onboard Telemetry
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Flapping wing aerial vehicles are nowadays in demand due to surveillance, civil needs, espionage and border missions.A lot of challenges exists in the development of autonomous flight missions for the flapping wing aerial vehicles which weigh less than 2 kg. This research focused on the development of data driven control system mathematical model and implementation on flapping wing platform in order to realize the autonomous flight. In this research,behavior of flapping wing aerial system is investigated using inertial measurement unit, barometer, GPS and wireless telemetry. In order to develop the mathematical model estimation as we utilized the real time telemetry data by doing flights in the fields. System parameters data was feed back to ground station with wireless telemetry which would do processing of the data to develop the mathematical model for the pitch, roll, yaw and height control behavior. Instead of relying on the theoretical mathematical models, which often are challenging to implement due to a lot complex mathematical calculations involved, system identification approach has been utilized and practically implemented with successful results.

articleTitle: A Novel Automated Steaming Machine for Mass Production of Aripahol
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: For years, steaming has been recognized as one of the healthiest ways to cook food with a major benefit being it locks in vitamins and flavors. This study aimed to develop an Arduino-based automated steaming machine for Aripahol, a well-known Filipino snack, to lessen the downtime of traditional production. This study focuses on designing and developing a low-cost steamer to improve production, reduce weight, and save labor for small and medium-sized enterprises. Current manual steaming processes are laborious, ineffective, and dangerous, given the exposure to steam. Although Aripahol found commercial steamers, none were cost-effective for small-scale businesses. To tackle these issues, the proposed steamer adds temperature and waterlevel features that are automated using an Arduino microcontroller to achieve optimal cooking. The machine can churn out 20 Aripohal per batch, which takes five minutes to cook, instead of the manual pace of making these items. We learned about the hardware components we could use, how to design circuits and some programming in Arduino IDE. In conclusion, according to the study, Aripahol production efficiency could be improved using an automated steamer. The findings support future research from the point of view of fine-tuning the machine's design and exploring its potential role in small-scale food production.

articleTitle: Paper Based Smart Sweat Sensor for Health Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: The paper presents a novel approach of noninvasive health monitoring using a paper-based smart sweat sensor. Human sweat is mainly water, containing a varied range of biomarkers such as electrolytes (sodium, potassium, chloride, ammonium etc.), metabolites, trace elements, neuropeptides, and cytokines. By leveraging image processing and machine learning (ML) techniques, the proposed system analyzes sweat samples by comparing the intensity of yellow color precipitates on filter paper strips due to a chemical reaction between sweat and a chemical reagent to determine electrolyte concentration in the sweat. We developed a model to predict health conditions based on input biomarkers such as pH, glucose, sodium, and potassium. In this study, apart from testing potassium concentration, the pH and glucose levels are synthetically assumed. The work was carried out to provide a simple, cost-effective, and reliable alternative non-invasive method for determining electrolyte (potassium) concentration in sweat for continuous health monitoring and predicting health condition. Following precise chemical analysis on collected sweat samples, accurate concentration of potassium (2.5mmol/ltr) is predicted through image processing. The proposed smart sweat sensor is a significant advancement towards the development of a non-invasive, simple and accurate wearable sensor in the future.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Algorithms vs SVPWM for Optimal Performance of MLI Driving Three-Phase Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: The performance of the three-phase multilevel inverter (MLI) is monitored and analyzed using genetic algorithm as an intelligent algorithm for solving mathematical equations accompanying the inverter operation. This performance is compared when employing the traditional space vector pulse width modulation (SVPWM) technique to drive the MLI. SVPWM is commonly used for applications in the power electronics field. The gating angles of the inverters are extracted using the selective harmonic elimination (SHE) concept for optimal switching using artificial algorithms and monitoring the performance of the inverter when loaded with a three-phase motor. Then monitoring the performance of the inverter when extracting these angles using SVPWM techniques. The inverter's voltages, currents, and load characteristics are analyzed, as well as the frequency analysis of the variables, while checking the active and reactive power levels injected to the load. A distinct advantage has been indicated for algorithmic technology compared to SVPWM technique for most variables. A detailed MATLAB model with reduced number of switches for three phase multilevel inverter is built and thoroughly analyzed for both techniques. Also, a practical 31 level single phase inverter is built for testing and measurement.

articleTitle: Capacitive Power Transfer with Capacitive Coupler Analysis on Vertical and Horizontal Aluminum Plate
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: According to references on Capacitive Power Transfer(CPT), research has mainly focused on a few key points: 1. Designing the compensation network components; 2. Designing aluminum plates for capacitive coupling, including considerations of plate length, area, number, and spacing; 3. Comparing CPT with Inductive Power Transfer. This paper uses Ansys Maxwell 3D to simulate the aluminum plates needed for CPT, comparing their performance in horizontal and vertical placements. In Section IV, we use PSIM simulations to compare the waveforms of these different plate orientations under an LCL-LCL high-order compensation structure.

articleTitle: Prediction of the Overall Effect of Cloud Cover on Power Quality of PV Solar Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: The shading effect due to cloud cover on PV solar power plants is a huge challenge in the maintenance of power quality. It can cause a power ramp down due to the movement of clouds in blue skies while the movement of clouds in a grey sky causes a significant loss of power in solar power plants. This paper presents a systematic approach for segmenting, tracking, and predicting the path of the clouds over the sky. It also develops a short-term solar energy forecasting model to predict the power output of the solar plant. The forecasting model uses real-time measurements to extract the average solar irradiance value and the power output of the plant for short-term prediction. The testing was carried out in a PV solar plant over one year. Within the implemented setup, the predicted power output cloud level and real-time video of cloud detection together with predicted power output are displayed on the Graphical User Interface. Accurate real-time detection, segmentation, and movement of distinct levels of cloud luminosity are presented. Extensive field trials showed promising results of meeting the stability requirements demanded by the regulating authority, from the large-scale grid tied PV solar plant operators. Hence authors expect the outcome will contribute towards migration into an integrated grid 4.0.

articleTitle: CNN Optimization for Bearing Fault Diagnostics in Adverse Industrial Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: In industrial environments, the reliability of machinery is often compromised by surrounding noise which can interfere diagnostic signals and lead to machine failures. Such failures usually result in unexpected downtime and considerable repair costs, emphasizing the need for more reliable diagnostic techniques. This study utilizes a CNN architecture to enhance fault diagnosis accuracy in noisy conditions. The proposed architecture is designed to extract informative features from complex vibration data even in the presence of substantial background noise. The optimization of CNN parameters is performed to maximize overall classification accuracy over various SNRs. The effectiveness of optimized model was extensively evaluated by using the CWRU Bearing dataset. The results show the accuracy of 88.89 % at the SNR of −4 dB and up to 97.96 % at the SNR of 10 dB. It demonstrates improvements over traditional fault diagnosis methods and can significantly reduce maintenance costs and enhance operational efficiency across industrial settings.

articleTitle: Study of a High-Efficiency WPT System with Dual Resonant Parameters Tuning Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Wireless charging for ships has been implemented in practical applications. However, due to variations in coupling conditions and margins of error, the system may experience detuning. While adjusting the frequency can maintain maximum efficiency on the receiver side, it also increases switching losses. To address this, this paper proposes a wide-frequency WPT system based on LCC-S compensation topology. The system incorporates variable inductor and variable capacitor techniques along with a dual-variable control method to ensure system stability during adjustments. Additionally, a sensorless foreign metal detecting technique is introduced, preventing safety from metal intrusion. A 300W WPT system prototype was developed to assess feasibility, and the results show that under horizontal and vertical misalignment variations of ±50% and +175<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, respectively, zero-voltage-switching (ZVS) was achieved in the resonant input, with system efficiency consistently above 86%, upon considering ESR.

articleTitle: Enhancing Battery's State of Health Estimation with Linear Models and Time- Energy Features
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Estimating the State of Health (SoH) is crucial for the safety and reliability of batteries, with accurate SoH estimation heavily relying on the selection of appropriate features. This paper proposes using time & energy features to enhance prediction accuracy. Experiments were conducted using the NASA Li-Ion dataset, which includes various batteries with different charging and discharging profiles. Feature extraction considered power during constant current (CC) and constant voltage (CV) charging phases, time features in the charging-discharging process, and temperature. A feature selection method was employed, and both nonlinear and linear approaches were optimized using GridSearchCV for SoH estimation. Results indicate that linear models (Lasso, ElasticNet, Ridge, SVR with a linear kernel, linear neural network, GPR with a linear kernel) outperform nonlinear models (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, nonlinear neural network, and nonlinear SVR & GPR kernels) in accuracy and generalization. Among all tested methods, linear GPR, Lasso, and linear SVR provided the most accurate predictions, demonstrating that with proper feature extraction, simpler regression methods can accurately and quickly estimate SoH.

articleTitle: Comparison of Full-Bridge and T-type DC/DC Converters for Electric Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: As the automotive industry is developing rapidly, electric vehicles (EVs) have become a popular idea for green transportation due to their zero tailpipe emissions. One of the key parts on the EV board is the isolated step-down DC/DC converter, essential for transferring power efficiently between the high-voltage battery and the low-voltage side while ensuring battery protection. This paper analyzes and compares the phase-shifted full-bridge (PSFB) and the T-type converters in terms of voltage and current stresses, losses, power density, and cost. Simulation and computational results indicate that the T-type converter with silicon-based middle switches achieves higher efficiency at lower power levels and is more cost-effective compared with the PSFB converter. Therefore, the T-type converter is a more efficient choice for powering the low-voltage side which requires lower power input in most cases.

articleTitle: Re-Engineering of Brainwaves to Increase Resistance to Distractions in Young Adults and Promote Optimal Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Deviation of attention or concentration from the current task is termed as distraction. Various psychological studies illustrate that distraction is valuable as far as it makes the person forget or escape from agony but also has destructive effects on the younger generation especially in maintaining focus, productivity, and achieving their career goals. This research focused on reducing distraction, especially in students studying under graduation. Audio photic brainwave entrainment using a Virtual reality device and noise-cancellation headphones is one of the effective ways to suppress task-irrelevant structures or distractions among young adults. This study was based on electroencephalograph signals from 14 healthy subjects. Initially, EEG signals were recorded from subjects under photic stimulation of 10Hz frequency. The Fast Fourier transform method was applied to electroencephalogram signals. The frequency band power ratios were observed, showing evidence that entrainment at alpha waves has synchronized the brain waves to alpha frequency and has reduced distractions by filtering out distractive sensory information. The topographical maps are also shown which supports the findings of the research.

articleTitle: A Predictive Economic Analysis Under Uncertain Scenario: Evidence Theory for Small-Scale Residential Community Power Network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Residential communities increasingly adopt renewable energy sources (RES) to reduce energy costs. However, these sources are weather-dependent and unpredictable, posing challenges for reliable operations. Therefore, managing uncertainties in power supply has become an important research focus. These uncertainties directly affect the performance of microgrids. Energy storage systems are integral, enabling battery-backed supply for residential loads during unpredictable conditions. This paper presents an evidence-based fusion framework for accurate load and PV power forecasting in uncertain scenarios. Dempster-Shaffer's theory has been used to develop a fusion framework. In addition, electricity network modeling for a day-long electricity cost analysis of a residential community has been done in three scenarios. In scenario 1, the community power supply is connected to the grid; in Scenario 2, users have a PV system on their premises but no storage; and in Scenario 3, users have their own PV-integrated storage system. The electricity price for buying and selling energy from the grid is also assumed to be fixed. The primary objective of this framework is to minimize the operating cost under a set of different constraints. The results showed that the prediction performance of the proposed algorithm is better than others. Thus, under uncertainty, scenario 3 is more economical than the other two, and the total cost with the proposed algorithm is less than $0.705 in scenario 1 and less than $0.339 in scenario 2.

articleTitle: Techno-economic Analysis of Hybrid Renewable Energy Storage Optimal Sizing in Urban Energy System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Advances in renewable energy systems have inevitably created opportunities like realizing self-sufficient and carbon emission-free energy systems and challenges such as optimal scheduling and sizing of single or multiple energy storages in energy systems. This study discusses the technical and economic objective functions for optimum sizing of renewable energy storage in the urban energy system i.e. grid and solar photovoltaic as the main power generation sources. It is perceived that leveraging energy storage according to the capability of each storage technology is the intelligent approach, as each storage technology comes up with some merits and demerits such as battery storage has a rapid response i.e. less than one second and higher round trip efficiency i.e. greater than 90% but it has a self-discharge rate of around 1% and capacity loss of 20%. As far as hydrogen storage is concerned it has a higher energy density but cycle efficiency of hydrogen storage is merely 50%. So, using these renewable storage technologies individually does not result in an efficient, economical, and reliable system. Thus, this paper analyzes the different combinations of these storage technologies into hybrid optimization by implementing, volatile grid electricity rates, limiting battery operation, precise battery and hydrogen usage, and limiting grid operation to achieve lowest energy cost, capacity shortage, and net present cost objective functions.

articleTitle: Design and Techno-Economic Feasibility Analysis of a 170kWp Rooftop Solar PV in a Health Facility
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: The healthcare sector is one of the most energy-intensive industries, with hospitals requiring a continuous and reliable electricity supply to operate critical life-saving equipment. In developing countries like the Philippines, high electricity costs, frequent power outages, and over-reliance on fossil fuels exacerbate these challenges, threatening both operational efficiency and patient care. This study conducted a techno-economic analysis of a 170 kWp rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) system installed at ACE Hospital in Butuan, Philippines. The analysis involved technical assessments to estimate energy production, system efficiency, and capacity factor. Economic viability was evaluated using metrics such as payback period, internal rate of return (IRR), and levelized cost of electricity (LCOE). Additionally, the environmental impact was assessed by calculating reductions in CO2 emissions and other pollutants. The system demonstrated high technical efficiency with an estimated annual energy production of 758,780 kWh and a capacity factor of 58.9%. Economically, the system exhibited a payback period of 3.97 years, an IRR of 26.1%, and an LCOE of PHP 2.30/kWh. Environmentally, the system is expected to displace 531,146 kg of CO2 annually. The findings indicate that the solar PV system is a viable and sustainable energy solution for healthcare facilities, offering significant economic savings and environmental benefits while enhancing energy security. This study supports broader adoption of solar energy in similar contexts.

articleTitle: Long-term Energy Demand Analysis using Machine Learning Algorithms: A Case Study in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: In each energy sector from production to consumption machine learning and statistical models have intimidated the power system for the past few decades. Among these, energy demand analysis is one of the approved research projects in Bangladesh due to its necessity. Such a study introduces energy consumption forecasting along with necessary environmental featured variables. These energy demands vary depending on short-term, medium-term, and long-term analysis. Although, this paper utilizes long-term energy demand research while predicting energy consumption. The dataset in the study includes three years of monthly data consisting of more than one million samples and diverse consumer types with versatile features of the capital of Bangladesh, Dhaka (mainly Uttara). Different machine learning models like; Random Forest, k-neighrest Neighbors regression, Extreme Gradient Boosting Method, and Light Gradient Boosting Method have been used and in order to evaluate them various performance constraints have been utilized. Among the models, KNN has performed considerably well. It has the result of about 0.9447 as R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, 163.9 as RMSE, and 28.7 as MAE. Such study will surely subsidize upgrading to the power system management of Bangladesh.

articleTitle: Performance Assessment of Classical Machine Learning Models Used for Entity Relationship Extraction on Online Philippine News Articles
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Content from legitimate online news articles is used to determine relationships of objects or entities to enable a more efficient way of extracting information. It could also be used to establish ground truths on news stories or current events to provide a reference against the emergence of fake news articles. This study involved the entity relationship extraction in an online news source, the Philippine Daily Inquirer online site Inquirer.net. Classical machine learning methods were designed to perform pairwise entity relationships via Semantic Web, and the performance of the methods was assessed and compared with one another in terms of training time and F1 scores. A 90–10 train-test split of data was used for each of the methods. A total of 12 machine learning methods were configured to accomplish the task of entity relationship extraction, and a total of 27 top entity relationships were obtained and ranked. The use of support vector machines (SVM) yielded the highest F1 score of 60.73% but took 592.54 seconds to complete the training. The fastest method to train was the multinomial naïve Bayes (MNB) at 0.63 seconds but only obtained an F1 score of 50.14%.

articleTitle: Real-Time Vehicle Tracking Mobile Application for University Campus Mobility Aid
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: The campus e-jeep system is intended to provide a convenient means of transportation within the campus. However, the lack of accessible ride information-such as the current location of e-jeeps, estimated time of arrival (ETA), and passenger count-often results in an inconvenient and inefficient experience for passengers. This study aimed to develop a cross-platform mobile application to enhance campus mobility by visualizing critical ride information, including e-jeep locations, station ETAs, and the number of available seats. To assess the application's user-friendliness, a prototype was tested by riders, which allowed the researchers to refine the application with a focus on improving the e-jeep riding experience. The application utilizes a database of near real-time e-jeep information stored in Firebase. The prototype was designed using Figma, and the mobile application was developed using several key technologies: Visual Studio Code, Expo Go, React Native, Tailwind CSS, and Google Maps. The application demonstrated 100% accuracy with an average latency of 414.7365 ms. It was also found to be scalable, capable of accommodating 10 e-jeeps and 500 simultaneous users. Finally, installer files for both Android and iOS were built and made available for download.

articleTitle: End to End Encrypted Messaging Application Using ORDEX
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: An end-to-end encrypted chatting application focuses on securely transmitting sensitive information. It prevents the intrusion of malicious parties with any ill intent. It is especially needed in organizations where employees exchange messages which may contain trade secrets. This paper discusses the use of OR Diffie Hellman Key Exchange (ORDEX) algorithm to transmit messages securely in chatting applications. Usually, there are multiple key exchanges and layers of security which slows down the application, to avoid this a faster key exchange algorithm is proposed which does not compromise on security. This paper proposes a key exchange algorithm which is a combination of ORDEX algorithm and Extended Triple Diffie Hellman (X3DH) [2] along with Double Ratchet [3]. Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) [1] encryption is used to encrypt the messages. The proposed solution is thousand times faster than applications using Elliptic-curve Diffie–Hellman (ECDH) [4] key exchange algorithm.

articleTitle: Internet-of- Things (IoT) - Based Automated Temperature Monitoring and Control System for Enhanced Cacao Fermentation Quality
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Cacao fermentation is critical for developing the chocolate flavor and quality. However, small-scale farmers often struggle to achieve consistent fermentation due to insufficient bean volumes and varying environmental conditions. This study focuses on the design and development of an Internet-of-Things (IoT)-based automated temperature monitoring and control system specifically for the cacao fermentation process. The system integrates a temperature sensor (DS18B20), a microcontroller (Arduino Uno), a heating element (nichrome wire), and a display unit (LCD) to maintain optimal fermentation temperatures. The system ensures consistent fermentation conditions by using artificial heat generation and real-time temperature adjustments. Testing demonstrated that the system maintains a steady-state error of ±0.15°C concerning the setpoint temperature. The automated control allows smallholder farmers to ferment smaller volumes of cacao effectively, ensuring the beans reach the desired quality standards. This technological advancement is expected to improve the overall yield quality and market value of cacao beans, benefiting the small-scale farming sector significantly.

articleTitle: Development of Real-Time Sensor Network for Characterization of Pyrolysis Oil from Waste Tires
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Pyrolysis, a viable method for producing valuable products like tire pyrolytic oil, addressing the environmental problems associated with the improper disposal of used tires. However, additional refinement is necessary to extract lighter fractions of the oil, which have higher economic value. This study focuses on the design and development of a small-scale atmospheric distillation system specifically engineered to characterize pyrolytic oil from waste tires. The system is designed to separate the lighter fractions of tire pyrolytic oil and analyze the distilled oil in accordance with ASTM standards, while also conducting physical and spectral characterization using a real-time sensor network. The real-time sensor network, which controls the system for characterizing tire pyrolytic oil, maintains precise temperature control within the 30-60°C range. It uses gravitydriven fluid movement, eliminating the need for mechanical pumps. Key parameters like density, pH level, and water content are carefully monitored and displayed on both a control panel and mobile devices. With the use of advanced sensors and calibration methods, the system ensures accurate measurements, addressing limitations found in existing technologies. The data collected during the oil characterization were compared with results from a standard testing laboratory in the Philippines accredited by the Department of Energy (DOE) using ASTM standards. These comparisons highlight the system's effectiveness in improving the reliability and usability of tire pyrolytic oil for various industrial applications. This innovative approach provides a cost-effective and efficient solution for refining tire pyrolytic oil and characterizing its physical and spectral properties, underscoring its significant potential for industrial use.

articleTitle: Hybrid Machine Learning Approaches for Robust Heart Disease Prediction: A Comprehensive Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: In addressing the global increase in prevalence of heart disease and its consequences for public wellness, this research emphasizes the need to have reliable prediction models. It is critical to promptly identify those who are at risk of cardiovascular disease to put preventive measures and appropriate treatments into place. In line with the World Health Organization (WHO), cardiovascular illnesses are responsible for a significant 31% of the world's mortality rate and cause an alarming 17.9 million deaths annually. Accurately assessing the severity of cardiac problems and forecasting their course is difficult due to the complicated clinical landscape, which is marked by intrinsic unpredictability and a complex interaction of components. As such, early detection becomes essential to the effective management of heart-related conditions. This study offers a thorough structure for forecasting cardiovascular illnesses by utilizing cutting-edge boosting strategies and machine learning approaches, such as Ada boost, Gradient boosting, CAT Boost, LG Boost, XG Boost and our proposed model together with GridSearchCV. With an emphasis on Early Heart Disease Prediction using Boosting-based ensemble Machine Learning Techniques, the motive of this research is to advance the creation of reliable models that can accurately predict the risks associated with cardiovascular health. Our proposed model with GridSearchCV is the best performer, according to the empirical results, with an accuracy of 99.8%. A comparative framework is given for all the methodologies. These findings highlight our model over competing algorithms with regard to their overall efficiency and anticipated accuracy, and they provide important new information for the field of cardiovascular health prediction.

articleTitle: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Control of Two-Tank Interacting System Using PID Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: A Single-Input Single-Output (SISO) interacting tank system is widely used in various industries for controlling liquid levels. It is a common setup in pharmaceutical industries where they store and mix chemicals. It is necessary to study the control of fluid levels in interconnected tanks to know the system dynamics and stability in feedback. In this paper, a system with two tanks is considered, each with different inflow and outflow rate, and the liquid levels in the tanks are influenced by the interaction between them. The liquid level data is collected from several experiments on the two-tank system and is modelled using System Identification (SI). A Proportional-Integral (PI) controller is used to regulate the liquid levels in the tanks by adjusting the inflow based on feedback. Reinforcement Learning (RL) is a booming technology used in industries because of it's ability to optimize complex decision-making processes, and good adaptability for different changing conditions without requiring a detailed mathematical model of the system. In this research, Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) and Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) RL agents are used to optimize PI tuning. The results highlight the performance of each agent in terms of reducing the settling time, rise time and the overshoot thereby enhancing the stability of the system. The performance metrics and error metrics for both TD3 and DDPG algorithms are observed. Rise time and settling time of TD3 is 8.63 sec and 25.74 sec respectively whereas for DDPG it is 26.81 sec and 79.92 sec, which is very high when compared to TD3. The comparison of error metrics namely ITAE, IAE and ISE show that TD3 has less error than DDPG. Overall, the experimental results conclude that TD3 is better for tuning a PID than DDPG.

articleTitle: Counting and Weight Estimation of Penaeus Vannamei Through Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Shrimp farming stands as a prominent and rapidly expanding sector of aquaculture in the Philippines, yet its sustainability is hindered by substantial feed costs, which represent a significant portion of total expenses for both small-holder and commercial farms. This study aims to address this challenge by developing an algorithm that accurately counts and estimates the weight of Penaeus Vannamei shrimps, thereby optimizing feeding patterns and fostering healthier growth. The research implements a measurement station with fixed lighting and camera height to generate a comprehensive dataset of shrimp images and corresponding weights. Utilizing YOLOv8 for detection and counting, coupled with supervised machine learning incorporating Area-based, Perimeter-based, Color-based, and GLCM-based estimation methods across multiple image batches. The study identifies Exponential GPR as the most effective regression model for the dataset. Furthermore, it reveals that Area-based and GLCM-based estimations exhibit the highest accuracy, with respective MSE, MAE, and R^2 values of 1.6814, 0.9005, 0.96 and 1.0638, 0.62359, 0.68. These findings offer valuable insights into optimizing efficiency and cost reduction strategies within shrimp farming operations, based on accurate counting and weight estimation algorithms.

articleTitle: Intrusion Detection on Industrial Networks Using Neuromorphic Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Cyber-attacks on Industrial Control Systems (ICS) present critical risks to operational stability, public safety, and national security. As industrial networks become more integrated and interconnected, their susceptibility to sophisticated cyber threats increases. Traditional security measures often fall short in detecting evolving attack patterns. This paper investigates the application of neuromorphic computing, which emulates the human brain's pattern recognition capabilities, as an innovative approach to intrusion detection in industrial networks. We introduce a hardware-based Spiking Neural Network (SNN) engineered to monitor and analyze communication packets in real time, detecting anomalies indicative of potential intrusions. The neuromorphic approach offers a promising solution to the growing challenge of cyber-attacks in critical infrastructure. The proposed system is implemented on an FPGA, focusing initially on monitoring key packet types such as LLDP, ARP, UDP, TCP, and Profibus RT, with scalability to accommodate additional protocols. The results demonstrate the efficacy of this SNN-based intrusion detection system in providing real-time, efficient, and accurate monitoring of industrial networks.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Different Intent Classification Algorithms for Agriculture Question and Answer Task
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: This research examines the effectiveness of various machine learning models in accurately classifying the intent of agricultural queries using fundamental machine learning techniques. The study analyzes two curated datasets: the QUERY dataset, containing 2,853 queries and their corresponding intents, and the ANSWERS dataset, which includes crops and their associated intents, covering 21 intent categories across 30 different crops. The main objective is to evaluate the performance of traditional machine learning models on this dataset to enable accurate intent classification, facilitating responsive interactions via the QA system, which delivers data-driven answers to farmers' queries. Notably, the Support Vector Classifier demonstrated the best performance with an accuracy of 92<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, closely followed by the Linear Discriminant Analysis Classifier. Using the Support Vector Classifier, the QA system efficiently retrieves responses from the ANSWERS dataset. This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of the performance of various algorithms for the question-answering (QA) task in the agricultural domain. The evaluation is based on pre-modelled classification reports from Sklearn's metrics package, ensuring rigorous analysis and detailed insights into the effectiveness of each approach.

articleTitle: Design of a Mini-Braille Cell Using Shape Memory Alloy-Based Actuators
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Refreshable braille displays (RBD) are electronic devices capable of outputting braille characters. However, these are larger compared to typical displays. RBDs that can be integrated into wearable devices or assistive devices can provide the blind and visually impaired (BVI) new alternatives to learn and navigate. This study explores a novel mini-braille cell design utilizing shape memory alloy (SMA) actuators. The SMAactuators were created from SMA wires that were programmed using a unique bending method. Subsequently, a PWM control scheme was utilized to regulate the SMA-actuators’ heat. The prototype was compared against an existing braille cell, the Metec P20 braille cell, wherein our prototype demonstrated almost 60% reduction in volume and is 25% lighter, measuring 25.5mm x 9.2mm x 8.1mm and weighing 3g. The output force of the raised braille dots was greater by 300% that can lift at least 75g of load. However, the refresh rate was slower, and heat transfer between activated and inactivated dots caused character display errors. These issues may be addressed in the future by improving the design and precision of the manufacturing of its components, particularly the SMA-actuators. Fine-tuning the control values could also improve the prototype's functionality. Index Terms—shape memory alloys, refreshable braille display, mini braille cell

articleTitle: On the Analysis and Application of Bio-Inspired Algorithms for Smart Navigation in Mobile Healthcare Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: In recent years, healthcare robotics has emerged as a promising solution to address the challenges of nurse burnout and shortages, while simultaneously enhancing patient care. Non-contact vitals monitoring has gained significance in reducing the spread of infectious diseases, exemplified by its role during the COVID-19 pandemic. Among various types of healthcare robots, wheeled mobile robots stand out due to their versatility and potential for autonomous navigation. However, achieving efficient and intelligent navigation in dynamic healthcare environments remains a complex problem. This paper examines behavior-based algorithms and evolutionary algorithms, which take inspiration from biological systems and swarm intelligence. Using these algorithms, the aim is to enhance the capabilities of healthcare robots, allowing them to navigate complex environments with ease and efficiency. This study encompasses an evaluation of popular healthcare robots, such as Dr. Spot, a non-contact vitals monitoring robot, and the versatile Temi robot. Through simulations using the Webots platform and the E-puck robot, we compare the performance of behavior-based and evolutionary algorithms. The results conclude the advantages of evolutionary algorithms in static environments. However, their limitations are observed in dynamic settings, where adaptation is crucial. The findings of this research offer guidance for designing and implementing autonomous wheeled mobile robots in real-world healthcare settings, where efficient and safe navigation is vital to ensure quality patient care.

articleTitle: A Review on Techniques for Power System Stability: The Role of Governor Setting Optimization and Algorithmic Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: When confronted with urgent issues, people often rush to implement solutions without fully assessing their long-term implications. This tendency can be seen in the current shift towards renewable energy amid increasing environmental issues and climate change concerns. While the pressure to embrace green technologies mounts, integrating renewable power sources into existing systems to curb carbon emissions poses significant challenges, notably in the area of power system stability mainte-nance. Although complex and sophisticated solutions are available to tackle system instability, implementation often encounters delays due to high capital costs and other complexities. Therefore, ensuring reliable operation of the power system becomes paramount until these solutions are effectively deployed. This article explores potential strategies for maintaining power system stability amidst renewable energy integration, with a focus on Governor Setting Optimization-a highly effective and swiftly implementable solution. Various algorithmic approaches for optimizing governor settings are discussed, along with a comparison of their pros and cons.

articleTitle: System Integration and Verification Approach for Large-Scale Space Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: When we define a large-scale system, a typical example would be a space development project. When we talk about large-scale systems in space development, there is the International Space Station (ISS), which was proposed by NASA in the 1980s as a manned space station, and which Japan, ESA, Canada, and later Russia joined as international partners. Japan's unique space transportation system, rocket development, began in the 1970s, and has a history of development of the H-1, H-2, and the new H-3, making it a largescale system promoted by Japan. In addition, the satellite carried on the third H-3 is called ALOS-4, which has an earth observation mission, and is a large satellite that weighs 3 tons and is 20 meters long when the solar paddles are deployed, so it can be said to be a large-scale system. In this paper, the author looks back on and explains the integration and verification of the International Space Station from development to operation, focusing on the development of large-scale space power systems, their integration, and verification. In addition, from a comparative perspective, the integration and verification of Japanese rocket development is compared with the ISS. The conceptual and basic design of the International Space Station began in the 1980s, and in-orbit assembly began in 1998. It is scheduled to be completed in 2011 and to end its role in 2030. Looking back at the history of the ISS, there are broadly a design phase, a development phase, and an assembly phase, and the operation phase began after in-orbit assembly began. In these phases, test verification and integration tests were conducted according to the phase at that time.
