The International Space Station, a large-scale space system, initially had an extremely high-risk assembly scenario in which elements and modules from each country were launched, connected in orbit, and element-to-element integration and verification tests were conducted for the first time. In this paper, the author describes how the problems and challenges of integration and verification of the International Space Station, an international collaborative program, have been solved, and attempts an overall evaluation of the development of such a large-scale system.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning Approaches In Open-Ended Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has traditionally excelled in well-defined environments with clear objectives and boundaries. However, the growing interest in open-ended environments, where the rules, goals, and dynamics can evolve or remain undefined, has posed significant challenges to conventional RL methodologies. This paper explores the adaptations and innovations in RL that address the unique demands of open-ended environments. Key approaches that we will examine include hierarchical reinforcement learning, intrinsic motivation-driven exploration strategies, meta-learning, and skill discovery without supervision. These methods are analyzed in conjunction with the open-ended goals of the study, which is to address the issues of complexity, uncertainty, and extensiveness inherent in considering the design of the open-ended systems. At the same time, we look at real-world uses in computer games, robotics, and autonomous systems, where RL is already used to deal with changing and uncertain environments. Lastly, we discuss the future directions of the work and the problems that are still not resolved, stating that there is a need for scalable solutions and a multidisciplinary approach in order to harness the maximum potential that RL demonstrates in open-ended situations.

articleTitle: Feature Engineering Techniques to Enhance Credit Scoring Models
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: This review article explores and evaluates the use of feature engineering techniques for clients' credit risk assessment through the development of methodologies involving machine learning algorithms. We use publicly available credit scoring datasets in both the development of our methods and for benchmarking. After describing the development of our methods, we present a discussion about the comparison of performances of our techniques and a number of other credit scoring methods described in the literature, including traditional statistical methods and advanced soft computing-based methods. One of the existing methods analyzed involves the use of evolutionary computing algorithms for feature selection and transformation. The development of an approach for credit scoring that integrates fuzzy neural networks with granular computing to handle data uncertainty and complexity. The main conclusion of this review is that feature engineering methods generally produced better results than traditional models, improving predictability and reducing variability of the outcomes. The performance of a combination of these techniques was highly satisfactory; the vagueness present in the information was effectively managed by our method, yielding improved results. From a practical perspective, although our methods have not proved to be substantially better than some market-available options, we demonstrated that it is possible for companies to develop credit scoring mechanisms internally using past data and advanced feature engineering techniques. Under certain circumstances, companies may find this option preferable to paying high fees to large credit scoring agencies for their proprietary systems.

articleTitle: Enhancing Robust Control of Irrigation Canal Systems with Quantitative Feedback Theory (QFT)
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Water, as a renewable resource, is critical for agricultural sustainability, yet managing its distribution through irrigation canals is complicated by uncertainties in hydraulic parameters, particularly the Manning roughness coefficient. While canal automation techniques improve system performance, traditional control strategies struggle with unknown variations, leading to inefficiencies. This paper presents Quantitative Feedback Theory (QFT) as a robust control strategy to address both structured and unstructured uncertainties in irrigation systems. Focusing on the Distributary-36, of the Tungabhadra Left Bank Canal (TLBC) system, we analyze the impact of ±30% uncertainty in roughness coefficients and design a QFT-based controller to maintain stability across these variations. Simulations show that the QFT controller ensures effective flow control and system stability, offering a more reliable solution for water management under fluctuating conditions.

articleTitle: Short-Term Prognostication of Solar Power Generation Using Hybrid VAR-CNN-LSTM Network Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: The modern microgrid contains various renewable energy sources that are intermittent. Due to the stochastic nature of the sources, it is essential to predict solar power for effective integration. The evolution of deep learning makes the prediction simple with complex and non-linear temporal data. In this paper, a hybrid Vector Auto Regressive (VAR) model, Convolutional neural network (CNN) and Long-short term memory (LSTM) are proposed to predict solar power using real-time data from Tamilnadu, India. The VAR-CNN-LSTM model employs the VAR model and deep learning network that combines CNN-LSTM layers to capture linear and non-linear data features. In this proposed hybrid method, the VAR model capture linear feature of the data, the CNN layer will extract the hierarchical structure from the various weather parameters, and LSTM will extract the long-term temporal characteristics of the data. The results obtained in this study for the proposed model is then compared with distinct VAR, CNN, LSTM, and hybrid CNN-LSTM models to verify the performance of the model.

articleTitle: Design and Development of an IoT-Based Load Monitoring Device for Three-Phase Building
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Efficient energy management in three-phase buildings requires real-time monitoring of electrical parameters. This paper presents the design, development, and implementation of an IoT-based load monitoring device integrated with a cloud-based data-logging system for a three phase building at the Caraga State University - Cabadbaran City. The study aims to enhance energy management by inspecting the existing electrical infrastructure, developing a real-time load monitoring device, and evaluating its accuracy and functionality. The device employs a 3-phase AC voltage sensor, KCT-36 split core current transformer, ESP32 microcontroller, and Arduino Uno R3 for data processing. Iterative calibration achieved voltage sensor accuracy with a negligible error of 0.01% and a maximum error of 2.18%, while current sensor accuracy showed a negligible error of 0.01% and a maximum error of 9.96%. Key findings include the device's ability to effectively visualize real-time data on voltage, current, and transformer loading through a web application. This system enhances maintenance and energy management, reducing power outages and equipment damage. The developed load monitoring device provides a scalable and cost-effective solution for academic, residential, and industrial settings, ensuring reliable and efficient energy use.

articleTitle: MSAF: A Multi-Scale Attention-Fusion Model for Long-Term Cell-Level Network Traffic Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Implementing precise network traffic prediction is essential for optimizing base station strategies, allocating network resources effectively, reducing costs, and ensuring service quality in network management. Currently, most mainstream forecasting methods primarily focus on either the time domain or the frequency domain, attempting to capture and express time series data features from a one-dimensional perspective. This one-dimensional approach can be limiting, as relying solely on a single dimension may lead to incomplete or suboptimal modeling, it fails to fully capture the intricate interactions between time-domain and frequency-domain that define network traffic behaviors. To address this, we propose a novel Multi-Scale Attention-Fusion (MSAF) model. The key module in MSAF, named Attention-Fusion, integrates both time-domain and frequency-domain features of network traffic data. This effectively addresses the limitations of previous attention mechanisms in simultaneously identifying frequency components and temporal patterns, providing enhanced modeling capabilities for complex network traffic data. Additionally, the Attention-Fusion module utilizes a DSConv module combined with the attention mechanism to identify correlations between sequences of different lengths. Evaluation of MSAF on two real-world network traffic datasets demonstrates that MSAF outperforms other mainstream methods in terms of forecasting performance.

articleTitle: The Effectiveness of Virtual Reality (VR)-Assisted Physical and Cognitive Rehabilitation on Stroke Recovery: A Mini Systematic Review
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Stroke is a leading cause of death and disability, requiring specific treatment strategies. Traditional methods often face limitations including accessibility, intensity, and patient engagement. This review evaluates the effectiveness of virtual reality (VR)-assisted rehabilitation in improving motor, cognitive, as well as psychosocial outcomes for its survivors. A search of PubMed, IEEE Xplore, ASME, Cochrane, and Scopus identified relevant studies published between 2019 and 2024. The eligible criteria included RCT and other similar studies focusing on the VR for stroke recovery. Data on study designs, its characteristics, intervention details, and outcomes were extracted and then synthesized. Three studies met the criteria and confirmed that VR improved motor recovery, cognitive function, and psychosocial well-being. In detail, a study concluded enhanced gait speed and motor coordination with combined tDCS and VR treadmill training. Another study demonstrated improvements in upper limb functionality and cognitive function by a diverse VR program, while another found gains in motor function, balance, and psychosocial wellbeing with VR and pharmacological treatment. In conclusion, VR improves motor, cognitive, and psychosocial outcomes significantly in stroke patients compared to a single conventional therapy. The immersive and interactive nature of VR enhances user engagement and adherence, offering a promising avenue for stroke rehabilitation.

articleTitle: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Based Large Language Model Chatbot for Improving Diagnosis for Physical and Mental Health
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Chatbot integration in the medical domain results in improved accessibility to healthcare information and services with enhanced patient query communication and patient education. The proposed work is a novel approach to Health Care chatbot named MEDGPT. The model is developed using the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework integrated with external data sources such as PDF documents, CSV files, and PubMed documents related to Health Care. It combines a retriever component of the architecture to fetch relevant information from external sources and a generator component to craft contextually appropriate responses using Large Language Model (LLM's). The architecture employed tools and agents in order to generate response from multiple external sources. Tools are specialized for each data source and are designed to extract relevant information based on user queries. Agents are components within the chatbot architecture that handle different aspects of logical reasoning and decision making. When a user query, requires information from an external data source, the corresponding agent invokes the appropriate retrieval tool. Once the data is processed, it is integrated into the chatbot's knowledge base using the RAG framework. The RAG framework combines the retrieved data with the chatbot's language generation capabilities to craft contextually appropriate responses to user queries. Through extensive testing and evaluation, the chatbot achieved significant improvements in user satisfaction, response accuracy, and engagement, showcasing the potential of the RAG framework in leveraging external data sources for intelligent conversational agents in Health Care. The proposed framework enhanced the RAG based LLM chatbot's capabilities to provide relevant and accurate responses to user queries related to Health Care with respected Physical and Mental health.
